caveats.detected_by: Looks for `[aria-label*="breadcrumb"]`, `.breadcrumb`, or `.breadcrumbs` on the page.
caveats.blind_spot: A breadcrumb implemented with different markup or class names is invisible to this check.
caveats.disprove: Open the screen and look at the top of the content area for a route-hierarchy trail before adding a new component.

caveats.detected_by: Looks for `input[type="search"]`, `[role="searchbox"]`, or `[aria-label*="search"]` inside the page's `header`/`nav`/`aside`/`[role="banner"]`.
caveats.blind_spot: A button that opens a search/command palette on click (rather than a visible text input) does not match any of those selectors, even though it provides the same capability.
caveats.disprove: Check this run's own UI inventory for a button labelled like "Search ..." in the topbar before building a new palette.

caveats.detected_by: Scans the first 50KB of page HTML for the literal substrings `ctrl`, `cmd`, or the ⌘/⇧ glyphs.
caveats.blind_spot: Shortcuts documented inside a help modal that loads lazily, or that use words like "hotkey" instead of ctrl/cmd, are missed.
caveats.disprove: Open any help/settings panel on the screen and check for a shortcuts list before adding one.

caveats.detected_by: Scans the first 50KB of page HTML for the literal substrings `help`, `tooltip`, or `info`.
caveats.blind_spot: Icon-only tooltips implemented via `title` attributes, custom popovers, or lazy-loaded content past the 50KB scan window can be missed.
caveats.disprove: Hover the non-obvious icon controls on the screen before adding new tooltip markup.

caveats.detected_by: Looks only for `[data-company-selector]`, `[data-branch-selector]`, `[data-fy-selector]`, or a native `<select name*="company|branch|financial">`. Fires on any screen whose title matches /book|invoice|gst|hrms|payroll/, including pre-login screens.
caveats.blind_spot: A custom button-based dropdown (e.g. a topbar button showing the company name, branch, or financial year that opens a menu on click) is structurally invisible to this check, and the check does not require the screen to be an authenticated app shell.
caveats.disprove: Check this run's own UI inventory for topbar buttons showing a company name, "HO"/branch code, or a year range (e.g. "2026 - 27") before adding a new selector. Also confirm the screen is actually an authenticated, multi-company screen and not the pre-login landing page.

caveats.detected_by: Requires a visible table (`meta.tables > 0`) and the literal word "export" nowhere in the page's visible text.
caveats.blind_spot: An export action rendered as an icon-only button, inside an overflow/kebab menu, or using different wording (e.g. "Download list") is missed.
caveats.disprove: Open any row-action or toolbar overflow menu on the table before adding a new Export control.

caveats.detected_by: Requires a visible table and neither the literal word "print" nor "download" anywhere in the page's visible text.
caveats.blind_spot: Print/Download actions behind an overflow menu or expressed with icon-only buttons are missed.
caveats.disprove: Check the table's row and header action menus before adding new Print/Download controls.

caveats.detected_by: Requires a visible table and zero elements matching `select`, `[role="combobox"]`, `.filter`, or `[class*="filter"]` on the page.
caveats.blind_spot: A custom filter bar built from plain buttons, chips, or a search box (with no matching class name) is invisible to this check.
caveats.disprove: Look for date-range, status, or search controls above the table before adding a new filter bar.

caveats.detected_by: Counts visible buttons sharing an identical accessible label/text; flags any label repeated more than twice.
caveats.blind_spot: When the shared label is a form-field placeholder (e.g. "— select —", "Select", "Choose"), the buttons are usually distinct per-field controls whose *visible copy* is intentionally identical; renaming the visible text would break the design system rather than fix an ambiguity.
caveats.disprove: If the duplicated label is a placeholder-style string, the fix is almost always a per-field accessible name (`aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` pointing at the adjacent field label), not new visible copy. Confirm before changing any on-screen text.

caveats.detected_by: Compares the widest visible table/modal's bounding-box width or height against the viewport at capture time.
caveats.blind_spot: A container with its own internal `overflow: auto` scroll region can still measure wider/taller than the viewport at the outer level, producing a false positive.
caveats.disprove: Resize the browser and check whether the table/modal already scrolls internally before adding a new scroll container.

caveats.detected_by: Flags the page whenever any console event of type `error` or `pageerror` was captured, regardless of cause.
caveats.blind_spot: A resource-load 404 (e.g. a missing optional avatar/logo image) triggers a browser console error identical in shape to a real script exception, and is not itself a functional regression.
caveats.disprove: Read the actual console message. If every flagged event is a 404 for an image/logo/asset URL, the fix is a graceful client-side fallback (skip the request, or catch the load error and show a placeholder), not a JavaScript bug hunt. Also check whether the failing request's host/path is owned by a different repository than the one this prompt names.

caveats.detected_by: Counts failed (`ok: false`) network requests captured during page observation, on the page's own URL, regardless of which host or path the failing request itself targeted.
caveats.blind_spot: Ownership is resolved from the *page* URL, not the *failing request* URL. If the product's API lives on a different host/path prefix than its frontend, the finding lands on the frontend repository even when the failing endpoint belongs to the backend repository.
caveats.disprove: Check the failing request's own URL against the repository ownership rules before assuming this repository owns the fix. A 404 on an optional asset (avatar, logo) usually only needs a frontend fallback; a 5xx on a data endpoint is a backend defect.

caveats.detected_by: Looks for legacy markup: `table[border]`, `font`/`marquee`/`blink` tags, `[bgcolor]`, `img[align]`, or `<center>`.
caveats.blind_spot: A modern component that happens to render one of these attributes for a legitimate reason (rare) would be a false positive; conversely, legacy styling done purely in CSS without these tags is missed.
caveats.disprove: Confirm the flagged markup is actually legacy-authored, not a modern component's incidental output, before migrating anything.

caveats.detected_by: Regex-matches page text for phrases like "no records", "no ... selected", "nothing here", or "select a ... to ...", only on authenticated screens with zero visible tables.
caveats.blind_spot: Any short sentence coincidentally matching the pattern (not actually a fallback state) would be misclassified; a genuine fallback state whose wording falls outside the pattern is missed.
caveats.disprove: Confirm the screen is genuinely blocked waiting for a prerequisite (company/branch/FY selection, no data yet) rather than a normal empty list.

caveats.detected_by: Manual/heuristic probe of `<input type="date">` fields; flags any native date input, since its displayed order follows the browser's locale rather than the product's.
caveats.blind_spot: None significant — this is a real product-level inconsistency risk on any native date input, independent of which locale a given tester's browser was pinned to.
caveats.disprove: Verify the exact field names/labels named in the finding still use native date inputs before building a custom date control.

caveats.detected_by: Compares an uploaded/exported fixture file's content and structure after a round trip through the product.
caveats.blind_spot: A fidelity mismatch can originate in the upload path, the export/render path, or the storage layer; the finding does not localize which one.
caveats.disprove: Reproduce the round trip locally and bisect which stage (upload, storage, export) introduces the mismatch before changing code.

caveats.detected_by: Splits the expected capability's display name into whitespace tokens and requires every token to appear (as a whole word, or substring for longer tokens) somewhere in the observed inventory's labels/URLs/hrefs. Any single missing token — even a near-synonym of a token that *did* match — keeps the whole capability unobserved.
caveats.blind_spot: A capability that exists under a different name, or whose route/label doesn't contain the literal expected word, is reported as `partial`/`implement` even when fully present. `matched_context` in the evidence lists exactly which tokens were found; anything not listed there was never seen anywhere in the run's inventory, on any screen.
caveats.disprove: Compare `matched_context` in the evidence against the full expected-feature name. If the missing tokens are near-synonyms of ones already matched (e.g. "employee" matched but "directory" did not, for "employee directory"), search this repository directly for the capability by its actual route/component name before implementing anything.

caveats.detected_by: The expected capability's tokens matched nowhere in the run's inventory, and the capability's name has no token overlap with the current session's scope, so this run has no first-hand evidence about it either way.
caveats.blind_spot: Zero evidence is not evidence of absence — the capability may live in a module this run never visited.
caveats.disprove: This is a scope question, not a defect. Confirm with the product owner before opening any implementation ticket; do not treat this as a build order.

fallback.detected_by: A generic heuristic check specific to this finding's category.
fallback.blind_spot: Heuristic DOM/text checks cannot see every valid implementation of a capability.
fallback.disprove: Verify directly against the live screen and this repository's code before implementing anything.
